name: AL-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans about 17 points Republican and incumbent Gary Palmer was renominated
Palmer holds a massive fundraising edge ($1.1M raised vs. roughly $30K for Maurice Mercer)
Prediction markets price the Republican at about 97 percent
No public polling; outlook rests on fundamentals and resources
model.rationale: The district's strong Republican lean, Palmer's incumbency, and his roughly 35-to-1 fundraising advantage all point the same direction, and prediction markets agree at about 97 percent Republican. With no polling or expert ratings suggesting any vulnerability, this stays firmly in Safe R territory.
model.watch: Only a late influx of Democratic outside spending or an unexpected scandal involving Palmer would give Mercer a realistic path, however narrow.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's 6th District, covering the Birmingham suburbs, leans heavily Republican, and incumbent Gary Palmer is seeking another term after securing renomination. No general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, candidate resources, and market pricing. Palmer has raised about $1.1 million and holds a large financial edge, while Democrat Maurice Mercer has raised roughly $30,000 with minimal cash on hand. Prediction markets give Republicans roughly a 97 percent chance of holding the seat.

The district's partisan lean of about 17 points Republican, combined with incumbency and the fundraising gap, makes an upset highly unlikely. Barring an unexpected development, Palmer is positioned to win comfortably in November.
